title: PMSM field-oriented control: transforms, current loops, decoupling, voltage limit
algorithm: Clarke/Park transforms, dq PI current control with decoupling, SVPWM (min-max), speed PI
plant_model: PMSM dq model, averaged inverter, RK4

status.software: Executed from a clean kernel; local unit tests passed at build time; GitHub Actions has not been run on this repository

limitations: Averaged inverter: no PWM ripple, dead time, switch drops or current-sensor error.
Surface magnets (Ld = Lq), no saturation, no iron loss, no cogging.
Ideal rotor angle and phase-current measurement.

checks.name: balanced set of amplitude 7: |alpha,beta| = 7 and dq = (7, 0) at its own angle
park/inv_park and clarke/inv_clarke round trips (error < 1e-12)
three-phase power equals 1.5 (vd id + vq iq) for zero-sequence-free sets
SVPWM: duties within [0,1] and the realised vector equals the request up to 0.99 Vdc/sqrt3
SVPWM shortens a request 5% above Vdc/sqrt3 (scale < 1) and keeps duties valid
voltage utilisation: SVPWM linear limit / sinusoidal PWM limit = 2/sqrt(3)
dq steady state equals the algebraic solution (id, iq within 0.5%)
electrical power = copper loss + mechanical power at steady state (error < 0.5% of the largest term)
dq from measured phase currents equals the model state (max error < 1e-9 A)
current-loop rise time at standstill within 25% of 2.197/wc
decoupling cuts the d-axis excursion after a 5 A iq step by at least a factor 3 (200 rad/s)
speed loop: zero steady-state speed error before and after the load step (<0.2%)
steady iq equals (Tl + B w)/kt within 2% and id is below 0.05 A
torque-producing current stays within 10% of the 10 A limit
commanded voltage magnitude never exceeds the linear limit Vdc/sqrt3
at the voltage limit the controller reports saturation
steady state at the limit: the algebraic voltage of the measured (id, iq, w) equals Vdc/sqrt3 (<1%)
steady state at the limit: iq equals B w / kt (within 0.02 A)
speed equals the voltage-limit root evaluated with the measured id (within 2%)
the limiter pushed id negative (unintended field weakening, id < -0.5 A)
